findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] `.panel` is not a child of `.contents`, so the new flex container does not affect it; removing `float: right` leaves it in normal flow and causes the header panel to stop right-aligning.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: removing `float: right` from `.panel` causes it to stop being right-aligned. The golden comment specifically mentions this affects the non-Ember/noscript header where `.panel` is nested inside `.row` and not a flex item. The candidate comment makes essentially the same point - that `.panel` is not a child of the flex container (`.contents`), so the flex layout doesn't affect it, and removing the float causes it to stop right-aligning. Both identify the same bug about the panel losing its right alignment due to the float removal.
